description: Clone any viral video with AI agents. Not just a script, the whole workflow: swap the face, the words, the B-roll, ship 100 variants in one command, and get your 100M views.
summary: The interesting part of Hypit isn't the "clone a viral video" pitch — it's SVML, a declarative video-workflow language that a coding agent writes and a local Chromium-based renderer compiles, with timing anchored to words rather than timestamps and generation models fully optional. That word-anchored, agent-writable intermediate representation is the kind of composable, observable pipeline I'm after, and the fact that it plugs into the same Claude Code / Codex loop I'm already wiring up in PenguPool makes it a useful reference for giving an LLM a structured output format a deterministic pipeline can execute. I'll grant them one thing: the architecture is sound even if the "100M views" tagline made me wince.
